text:
lucy: FYI customers hitting weird header variants that break our SDK backoff. Some proxies send `x-rate-limit-reset-ms` vs our parser expecting `x-ratelimit-reset-ms` or `Retry-After`.
ryan: ouch. I found a case where header had a stray hyphen: `x-rate-limit-reset-ms` and value was epoch ms. parse failed -> immediate retry -> more 429s.
anya: can we make parsing tolerant? plan: case-insensitive keys, strip punctuation, accept `-ms` epoch vs seconds, accept `quota-remaining`/`x-ratelimit-remaining`.
cheng: +1. Also propose a small RateLimit dataclass in sdk.types: `limit:int|None`, `remaining:int|None`, `reset_at:float|None`. Expose it on Response.meta['rate_limit'] and return from parser util.
lucy: also want a client-side soft-throttle util (token-bucket) that uses RateLimit to avoid storming when remaining=0. Keep it optional behind SDK flag.
ryan: for async clients, implement `async def retry_with_backoff(fn, *, retries=4, base_delay=0.25)` that inspects headers, uses `reset_at` if present to compute sleep, otherwise exponential. returns last response or raises.
anya: typing: add .pyi stubs and overloads so mypy knows retry_with_backoff is async and returns sdk.Response. Use TypeVar to accept any call signature.
ci-bot: opened issue #4199: "py-sdk: tolerant rate header parsing + optional token-bucket soft-throttle" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4199)
lucy: i'll draft a tiny spec in the issue with header canonicalization rules and example aiohttp snippet. can someone pick up tests?
ryan: i'll write unit tests for header permutations and token-bucket behavior. include integration with fake server returning alternating header variants.
cheng: will review typing PR.
lucy: thanks team :thumbsup: end.
